messages:
jen: Heads-up: i opened a small PR to tidy SDK examples for streaming/pagination across py/ts/go. main goals: consistent "cursor" naming, show proper stream cleanup, and add a short note about processing concurrency. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/docs/pulls/856

ryan: pinged. which examples are changing?

jen: docs/sdks/python/streaming.md, docs/sdks/ts/streams.md, docs/sdks/go/pagination.md and a tiny utils snippet in docs/sdks/common/retries.md. also swapped out continuation_token -> cursor everywhere in examples.

manuel: agree with the cursor rename. runtime payload uses "cursor" and the SDKs should mirror that. also, can we show explicit close patterns? folks copy/paste and forget to close streams in long-running processes.

jen: added variants: python async iterator with try/finally + await aclose(), ts for-await-of with stream.close(), and go pattern using defer stream.Close(). put a short table listing the method names per SDK.

ryan: can you paste the python example you added? i want to check wording.

jen: pasted snippet:
```python
async def read_stream():
    stream = await client.stream.create(model="small", input="hi")
    try:
        async for chunk in stream.generate():
            # process without awaiting if heavy
            queue.put_nowait(chunk)
    finally:
        await stream.aclose()
```

manuel: looks good. add a comment about not awaiting inside the loop to avoid serializing the pipeline and to use a worker pool.

jen: done. for TS i used:
```ts
const stream = await client.stream.create({model: 'small', input: 'hi'})
for await (const part of stream) {
  workerPool.enqueue(part)
}
await stream.close()
```

ryan: nit: call it close() in the TS example and mention it's the counterpart to Python's aclose() — i added a small inline note. also flagged an instance in go/pagination.md where the struct used ContinuationToken instead of Cursor.

jen: fixed the Go snippet to use Cursor and a loop that updates req.Cursor = resp.Cursor. also added a short paragraph: "treat cursor tokens as opaque; don't try to interpret them; changing page_size may affect token validity".

manuel: can we add one-liner retry snippet? i prefer showing RetryHelper usage so teams can copy the pattern.

jen: added a small pseudo-example under retries/common:
```python
from redwood import RetryConfig
rc = RetryConfig(max_retries=4, backoff='exp')
with client.with_retry(rc):
    for page in client.paginate(...):
        handle(page)
```

ryan: nice. also updated the link to the public pagination spec (was pointing to an internal doc). changed to https://docs.redwood.ai/runtime/pagination. 

docs-bot: [auto] Added task: update SDK changelogs + add crosslink to runtime param reference.

manuel: one more thought: add a quick note on idempotency for pagination calls and mention not to rely on stable ordering across pages unless ordering params were requested. tiny sentence should do.

jen: added that. okay to merge once one more person approves?

ryan: approved. merging now. thanks for moving this along.

jen: merged. i'll follow up with a small follow-up PR adding example tests that assert streams are closed and paginators handle empty cursors. cheers!
